title: Vortex four-week instructional entry map
scope: Stage 2 architecture only: twenty deliberately authored instructional offerings. This is not twenty required attendances, a completed workout curriculum, a medical clearance, or a completed separate tumbling program.

delivery_contract.instruction_budget: Demonstration, correction, recovery, water, equipment and transitions remain inside the component clocks. Reduce optional work and task count to create teaching time. Never shorten required recovery to finish a lesson.
delivery_contract.age_readiness_rule: Every age band needs its own exact prescription later. Current eligibility follows task competency, training history, attention, readiness and restrictions independently of age. New older athletes may need instruction; experienced younger athletes may bypass it. No absolute group load or advanced skill is unlocked by age.
delivery_contract.logistics_assumptions: Initial feasibility model only: 15 athletes, three lanes, two qualified athletic coaches. One coach demonstrates/observes the current new skill while the other supervises familiar practice and traffic; serialize unfamiliar work rather than running multiple unobservable teaching stations. Actual line of sight, equipment counts, run-off and coach availability remain unverified. Separate tumbling staffing is an additional unresolved dependency.

standard_preparation.instruction_rule: Retain the recognizable ordered base and finish it with hinge and squat observations. Use mastered drill levels and teach missing pieces over visits; the full list is not a quota. In compressed delivery rotate optional carioca and B/C-skips into appropriate visits rather than rushing them. Exactly two targeted athletic preparation purposes are authored in each entry: position/movement rehearsal, then progressive explosive-task rehearsal. Later prescription must resolve actual age-scaled drills and prove timing.

delivery_contract.full_body_rule: Each visit retains appropriate knee, hip, push, pull and brace exposure. The named emphasis receives the teaching/development attention; other patterns can use small familiar practice roles. A problematic pattern uses a suitable supervised regression without canceling productive work elsewhere.
delivery_contract.final_window_rule: The booked window supports reflection, recovery, low-fatigue engagement or the tumbling readiness handoff. It is not compulsory conditioning or a fifth pillar. Count any later prescribed work; no catch-up contacts or fatigue challenge before tumbling.
delivery_contract.tumbling_rule: Every entry gives a separate handoff objective, not a thirty-minute prescription. The approved managed session, skill prerequisites, mats, space and qualified staffing are unresolved. The tumbling coach decides the eligible foundation. Fatigue may require familiar foundations; unfamiliar advanced skills need fresh separately planned practice. Athletic entry never approves advanced tumbling.
delivery_contract.canonical_status: All named anchors and methods below are provisional planning families. No canonical IDs, current facility approval, equipment availability or matched media are asserted. Resolve these after the complete outline audit; propose any true missing card through the existing approval process.
delivery_contract.safety_and_quality: Coach observes comfortable execution and attention. Stop or modify for pain, dizziness, distress, restrictions or materially altered mechanics; follow the facility and qualified-professional process. Hold or simplify when quality is inconsistent; a fatigued check is deferred rather than recorded as failure of an enduring competency.
delivery_contract.first_visit_rule: Familiar means previously documented or demonstrated competent today. A first-time athlete without established patterns receives direct, serialized demonstration of simple supported full-body variants; never assume independent circuit readiness. Simplify variants, remove optional content and lower teaching ambition to preserve safe basic roles within the clock. Detailed feasibility must prove that this can be supervised; the outline does not claim the first visit already fits.

attendance_and_entry_policy.calendar: Four weeks of five offerings organize teaching availability. An athlete progresses from demonstrated work, not from elapsed weeks, age, or number of visits.
attendance_and_entry_policy.direct_entry: Before bypass, verify universal participation domains and the exact simple variations needed by the current main session. Accept recent documented evidence with current readiness checks. Unknown is not passed. No forced retesting of every mastered domain.
attendance_and_entry_policy.partial_entry: Admit a documented suitable main variation while targeting remaining gaps only when supervision and that session permit. If a missing domain prevents safe participation, retain supervised instruction for that task. Do not place the athlete in unsupported independent stations.
attendance_and_entry_policy.lower_frequency: At each actual visit prioritize the missing domain needed next, retain brief familiar full-body/explosive practice, and carry the unresolved modules forward without adding missed workload. Fixed-weekday attendees may be directed to a relevant module/check within their visit; never wait for the same lesson to recur on the calendar.
attendance_and_entry_policy.frequent_attendance: Use low-demand learning and retained pattern practice between substantive exposures. Count sport and tumbling as well as gym work. Even an instructional session may add fatigue; reduce attendance when the whole schedule lacks recovery.
attendance_and_entry_policy.recording: For every observed domain record athlete, date, offering ID, exact observed variation, setup/conditions, cue/support needed, status, readiness and actual completed work once prescribed. Status vocabulary: unobserved, needs_instruction, emerging, repeatable, modified, restricted. Record coach and next action. Outline plans are never actual results.
attendance_and_entry_policy.pass_rule: A qualified coach observes repeatable execution at the intended simple variation across separated opportunities with required control, cue understanding and recovery behavior. A single lucky effort or self-report is insufficient. Exact exercise-level criteria await canonical mapping; no universal numeric test is invented.
attendance_and_entry_policy.main_handoff: Record the matched current main session ID, eligible variation, most recent actual instructional exposure, unresolved restrictions, appropriate starting dose once prescribed, and next conditional exposure. Main calendar week never grants a progressed dose. Main-family links below identify eligible demand, not an exact unverified Day number.

weeks.objective: Learn safe group participation while establishing controllable starts, landings, stops, basic running rhythm and full-body strength patterns.
weeks.review: Record what is already repeatable and what needs instruction; do not require an experienced newcomer to repeat the entire week.

weeks.objective: Repeat the entry patterns with less prompting; learn appropriate load selection, recovery behavior and controlled changes of direction.
weeks.review: One demand changes only when its prerequisite is repeatable; frequent attendees retain low-demand alternatives.

weeks.objective: Use known skills within normal station flow and add an early, simple decision only to an already controlled movement.
weeks.review: Audit independent decisions about space, rest and stopping, while identifying domain-specific main-entry options.

weeks.objective: Verify the simple main-family variations under repeatable conditions and transfer an honest competency record into the current main offering.
weeks.review: Review only unresolved domains, respect fatigue and release eligible variations individually; elapsed week four does not force graduation.

entry_domains.observable_check: Respond to stop/start, wait for a clear travel and return lane, move/park equipment only on instruction, maintain spacing, and report symptoms.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Supervised normal group/station participation; this gate applies to every family.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Use directly supervised orientation or a serialized station until conduct is repeatable; no independent release into active traffic.

entry_domains.observable_check: Follow the recognizable base at a mastered drill level; complete comfortable hinge/squat checks and understand the two task-specific rehearsals.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: The current main preparation at an eligible drill level, with targeted teaching where necessary.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Keep base identity, teach the missing piece, substitute a mastered drill level and record the regression.

entry_domains.observable_check: Organize the selected start, accelerate within the clear lane and finish through the allocated controlled run-off without racing the stopping boundary.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Familiar short acceleration and a known straight-line response task; no resisted, overspeed or complex starts implied.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Reduce start/approach demand and directly coach the route; failed run-off control prevents faster exposure.

entry_domains.observable_check: Land the eligible simple jump with balance and comfortable control; separately demonstrate throw direction, release permission and safe retrieval.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: JUMP permits a separately passed simple jump-and-stick. JUMP-T permits a familiar stable throw while landing remains instructional, only after independent handling, stance, direction, release, retrieval and conduct checks pass. REACT-T additionally requires its actual early cue rule to pass; a throw pass does not pass landing or go/no-go.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Keep landing remediation separate. Consider JUMP-T only with its independently passed stable-throw gate; a failed landing does not authorize throwing. If throw handling is also emerging, continue supervised instruction instead of the main throw branch. Do not add rebounds.

entry_domains.observable_check: Slow and stop from the selected approach; for a planned redirect, place/reload the stance and leave the known route without losing balance.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Controlled straight stop first; a predictable modest redirect only when that separate check passes.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Shorten or slow the approach, remove direction change, and withhold reactive cutting until predictable control is demonstrated. On a relevant main REACT offering, REACT-T may replace travel only after separate stable-throw and early-cue checks pass; a braking gap alone grants no throw permission.

entry_domains.observable_check: Recognize the start, buildup and run-off areas; show comfortable upright rhythm through a progressive run while staying in lane and accepting full recovery.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Progressive upright running only with verified space; this is not proof of readiness for maximal-velocity sprinting.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Use labeled short acceleration or throwing if space is insufficient; technical rhythm practice alone does not count as top-speed exposure.

entry_domains.observable_check: Recognize an early cue, make the correct simple choice, and preserve the already demonstrated stop/throw/travel behavior.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: REACT-T permits a familiar stable throw on the separately passed early release or go/no-go rule while travel/braking remains instructional. A passed release cue does not pass withholding on a no-go cue. A traveling directional response still requires its own movement and cue checks.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Remove the unpassed cue demand and retain only a documented simpler release rule with the stable-throw gate met. If no early cue rule is passed, REACT-T remains instructional. A cue/throw result is never a reactive-cut result.

entry_domains.observable_check: Repeat the chosen knee, hip, push, pull and brace variations through a comfortable controlled range; follow setup, load, equipment and stop instructions.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Pattern-specific simple full-body strength variations with the documented effort/load choice; never a blanket advanced lift permission.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Use a supported or simpler variant in only the limiting pattern and preserve other eligible work; unresolved handling/supervision blocks independent loading.

entry_domains.observable_check: Distinguish quality output from fatigue work, wait for the assigned restart, stop when instructed, describe readiness and accept a held/reduced prescription.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Participation in counted, coach-prescribed output and strength work with its actual recovery.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Keep coach-managed release and simple tasks; remove competitive pressure and do not reward more attempts.

entry_domains.observable_check: Tumbling coach records attention, support/orientation/landing eligibility and readiness for the selected foundational skill in the separate managed program.
entry_domains.simple_entry_unlock: Only the explicitly approved foundational body-control option; athletic competencies do not unlock advanced tumbling.
entry_domains.if_incomplete: Keep an approved floor-level foundation or defer the affected skill; the exact program and staffing must first be verified.

sessions.title: Enter the lane, start on purpose, finish under control
sessions.primary_objective: Learn the start/stop contract and establish an eligible acceleration and knee-pattern entry point.
sessions.quality_target: Athlete waits for release, uses the clear route and controlled run-off, and repeats a comfortable knee pattern without prompting every action.
sessions.supporting_maintenance_qualities: Spacing, balance, hinge awareness, upper-body practice and reporting readiness.
sessions.explosive_focus: Coach-released short acceleration
sessions.full_body_strength_emphasis: Knee: teach comfortable squat pattern; hip: familiar supported hinge rehearsal; push: eligible inclined/support variation; pull: simple supported pull; brace: stable carry/support awareness.

provisional_anchors_methods.method: Direct demonstration and teach-back of lane rules; coach-released single-task practice with recovery; supervised pattern calibration. Exact approved methods, exercise variants and dosage remain unresolved.

sessions.progression_decision: Introduce route and one start; retain any demonstrated strength variation. Reduce output and task count while conduct is being learned rather than adding more instructions at speed.
sessions.prerequisites: No prior OR attendance required. Coach checks restrictions, ability to follow stop cues and comfortable supported movement before live lane travel.
sessions.observation_recording: Record conduct_flow, standard_preparation, acceleration_runoff and selected strength variations; separate already-mastered behaviors from unknown evidence.
sessions.exposure_link_rule: These IDs name relevant learning/check opportunities, not compulsory attendance. Use actual competency evidence; remedial routes can revisit a named earlier module without repeating its whole session.
sessions.workload_recovery: Instructional exposure with coach-controlled releases and generous recovery. For a fatigued arrival use walking route rehearsal and familiar low-demand strength; no timed race.

preparation.standard_base: Use delivery_contract.standard_preparation, preserve concluding hinge/squat checks and mastered drill levels.

targeted_drill_purposes.purpose: Rehearse start stance and stable knee/hip alignment shared by acceleration and the squat entry.
Progress the known start into a comfortable short acceleration and controlled finish only after the lane is clear.

sessions.final_window_role: Explain symptom reporting, water and the tumbling handoff; no extra sprint game.
sessions.separate_tumbling_interface: Introduce the separate tumbling coach and required attention/support checks; only that coach selects an approved floor-level foundation.
sessions.compressed_time_priorities: Preserve traffic teaching, hinge/squat checks, one acceleration task and all five strength roles; remove optional drill variants and use the final window for handoff.
sessions.partial_competency_lower_frequency_bypas: A competent newcomer may demonstrate route/control and move to OR-10 checks. A partial pass retains supported strength while traffic is directly supervised; lower-frequency visitors carry only the unresolved domain forward.
main_entry_unlocks: ACC: supervised simple acceleration and eligible knee emphasis once conduct, run-off and pattern checks pass.
sessions.advance_hold_reduce_rule: Advance only the named variable when the stated quality is repeatable and current readiness supports it; otherwise retain, simplify, reduce or defer the affected task. No calendar-based advancement or catch-up work.
sessions.age_and_library_override: Apply the shared age-readiness, safety and canonical rules. This outline contains no exercise-level age prescriptions and grants no unverified card approval.

sessions.title: Own a landing and distinguish the hinge
sessions.primary_objective: Teach force absorption through a simple landing and distinguish hip movement from the knee pattern.
sessions.quality_target: Athlete finishes the eligible jump balanced without chasing distance, and repeats the selected hinge with a comfortable stable trunk.
sessions.supporting_maintenance_qualities: Landing balance, ankle/hip coordination, retained start conduct and upper-body strength practice.
sessions.explosive_focus: Low-demand jump-and-stick
sessions.full_body_strength_emphasis: Hip: teach the hinge with an appropriate support or reference; knee: retain comfortable squat; push: familiar supported push; pull: familiar supported pull; brace: stable position without breath-holding instruction.

provisional_anchors_methods.method: Guided landing-position rehearsal and blocked practice of a consistent finish; contrast knee and hip movement through concise demonstration. Exact approved methods, exercise variants and dosage remain unresolved.

sessions.progression_decision: Introduce landing control and hinge distinction. Retain the known takeoff and other strength patterns; defer rebound or greater output while the finish is inconsistent.
sessions.prerequisites: Conduct and lane clearance from OR-01 or direct check; comfortable standing/landing preparation and eligible basic strength participation.
sessions.observation_recording: Record landing_throwing landing branch separately from throw competence; note landing balance, cue dependence and the exact hinge support used.
sessions.exposure_link_rule: These IDs name relevant learning/check opportunities, not compulsory attendance. Use actual competency evidence; remedial routes can revisit a named earlier module without repeating its whole session.
sessions.workload_recovery: Keep impact modest and separated by recovery. Replace repeated jump practice with non-flight landing-position rehearsal if yesterday, sport or tumbling has created fatigue.

preparation.standard_base: Use delivery_contract.standard_preparation, preserve concluding hinge/squat checks and mastered drill levels.

targeted_drill_purposes.purpose: Rehearse the hinge and quiet athletic finish so the athlete distinguishes hip loading from a deep squat.
Build from a small controlled takeoff/landing to the eligible jump-and-stick while retaining the same finish.

sessions.final_window_role: Reflect on a controllable landing; recover for tumbling instead of adding a jump competition.
sessions.separate_tumbling_interface: Report new landing exposure and observed balance; the separate coach chooses familiar floor orientation/landing foundations only when ready.
sessions.compressed_time_priorities: Protect hinge teaching and landing observation; use one landing task and familiar push/pull/brace roles, with no secondary jump family.
sessions.partial_competency_lower_frequency_bypas: A hinge pass with an emerging landing allows appropriate main strength. JUMP-T on a relevant main JUMP offering requires independently passed stable-throw handling, stance, release, direction, retrieval and conduct, checked through OR-05/OR-19 or direct evidence; landing failure does not grant that pass. Directly competent arrivals may use OR-06 or OR-19 checks.
main_entry_unlocks: JUMP: simple jump-and-stick if landing passes; a separately checked simple hinge variation for the main hip emphasis.
JUMP-T: familiar stable throw pending landing competence only after the separate throwing gate is documented; OR-02 landing failure alone does not qualify this branch.
sessions.advance_hold_reduce_rule: Advance only the named variable when the stated quality is repeatable and current readiness supports it; otherwise retain, simplify, reduce or defer the affected task. No calendar-based advancement or catch-up work.

sessions.title: Slow down before changing direction
sessions.primary_objective: Teach a deliberate straight stop and a supported unilateral stance before any redirect.
sessions.quality_target: Athlete reduces approach speed into a balanced stop inside the permitted area and controls the selected split stance on both sides.
sessions.supporting_maintenance_qualities: Balance, absorption, attention to stopping space and retained full-body strength.
sessions.explosive_focus: Predictable straight-line braking
sessions.full_body_strength_emphasis: Unilateral knee/hip: teach supported split stance; knee: retain squat awareness; hip: familiar hinge; push and pull: supported familiar variants; brace: steady trunk during stance.

provisional_anchors_methods.method: Predictable approach-to-stop practice with a complete reset; supported unilateral pattern rehearsal and immediate positional feedback. Exact approved methods, exercise variants and dosage remain unresolved.

sessions.progression_decision: Change from stationary landing to slow approach absorption. Retain a known route and remove cutting; approach speed is held until the stop is repeatable.
sessions.prerequisites: OR-01 conduct and OR-02 landing-position competence, or direct equivalents; no pain or restriction affecting the chosen stance.
sessions.observation_recording: Record braking_redirection straight-stop branch, bilateral stance observations and whether approach or support had to be reduced.
sessions.exposure_link_rule: These IDs name relevant learning/check opportunities, not compulsory attendance. Use actual competency evidence; remedial routes can revisit a named earlier module without repeating its whole session.
sessions.workload_recovery: Controlled low-speed exposures; no sprint-to-stop contest. Frequent attendees reduce landing/stop repetition and use supported stance practice.

preparation.standard_base: Use delivery_contract.standard_preparation, preserve concluding hinge/squat checks and mastered drill levels.

targeted_drill_purposes.purpose: Rehearse a comfortable braking stance and supported split stance with usable knee/hip alignment.
Progress from walking into the chosen straight stop while preserving the same balanced finish.

sessions.final_window_role: Review the difference between run-off and active braking, then prepare the handoff without extra shuttle work.
sessions.separate_tumbling_interface: Share landing/braking fatigue and stance control; the tumbling coach independently verifies floor support and orientation prerequisites.
sessions.compressed_time_priorities: Keep one stopping route, unilateral teaching and familiar full-body roles; defer any lateral introduction rather than shorten rest.
sessions.partial_competency_lower_frequency_bypas: Athletes who already stop consistently can check OR-07 redirection readiness; those with a unilateral gap retain supported strength. Infrequent visitors revisit only the failed approach or stance component.
main_entry_unlocks: BRAKE: controlled straight stops; no planned cut or reactive cut unlocked yet.

sessions.title: Find upright rhythm and understand the running corridor
sessions.primary_objective: Teach simple upright running rhythm and recognition of buildup and run-off boundaries.
sessions.quality_target: Athlete keeps comfortable rhythm within the lane, recognizes the controlled finish area and follows the familiar preparation at an eligible level.
sessions.supporting_maintenance_qualities: Coordination, mobility, preparation independence and balanced strength control.
sessions.explosive_focus: Upright rhythm into progressive running when space permits
sessions.full_body_strength_emphasis: Balanced knee and hip familiar patterns; push and pull receive equal teaching visibility; brace uses stable support or carry. No new loading emphasis.

anchor_families: Upright rhythm into progressive running when space permits
provisional_anchors_methods.method: Simple rhythm rehearsal into a progressive run; walk-through of the corridor; familiar balanced strength preserves teaching attention. Exact approved methods, exercise variants and dosage remain unresolved.

sessions.progression_decision: Introduce corridor awareness and simple rhythm while holding output. Retain familiar strength to reserve attention for running; no maximal-speed target.
sessions.prerequisites: OR-01 traffic/run-off control or direct check. Coach verifies a suitable corridor; rhythm competence alone cannot substitute for safe space.
sessions.observation_recording: Record standard_preparation, upright_running route/rhythm and actual space condition; if substituted, record acceleration or throw rather than top speed.
sessions.exposure_link_rule: These IDs name relevant learning/check opportunities, not compulsory attendance. Use actual competency evidence; remedial routes can revisit a named earlier module without repeating its whole session.
sessions.workload_recovery: Learning pace with full recovery. If consecutive visits or sport reduce coordination, retain walking/marching rhythm and lower-demand strength.

preparation.standard_base: Use delivery_contract.standard_preparation, preserve concluding hinge/squat checks and mastered drill levels.

targeted_drill_purposes.purpose: Rehearse comfortable upright posture and rhythm without excessive technical cues; connect stable trunk to balanced strength.
Build gradually into the permitted running route; if space is inadequate, progressively rehearse a labeled short acceleration.

sessions.final_window_role: Have athletes identify recovery readiness and the safe return route; no continuous running finisher.
sessions.separate_tumbling_interface: Share coordination and fatigue observations; use the separate approved foundational orientation lane, not new complex inversion.
sessions.compressed_time_priorities: Keep corridor instruction, compact familiar base, one progressive running task and balanced strength; omit secondary rhythm drills.
sessions.partial_competency_lower_frequency_bypas: Competent athletes may check OR-08 directly. Limited space does not fail the athlete but leaves upright-running permission unobserved; use eligible main alternatives until a suitable space check occurs.
main_entry_unlocks: RUN: controlled progressive running when space and route checks pass; otherwise a clearly labeled acceleration alternative after its own check.

sessions.supporting_maintenance_qualities: Perception, coordination, equipment conduct, trunk control and retained low-demand lower-body patterns.
sessions.explosive_focus: Stationary throw on a known release cue
sessions.full_body_strength_emphasis: Push/pull: teach matched stable upper-body patterns and setup; knee: familiar squat; hip: familiar hinge; brace: stable throwing/support position.

anchor_families: Stationary throw on a known release cue
provisional_anchors_methods.method: Stable throw task with controlled release/retrieval; teach push/pull setup separately before normal station flow. Exact approved methods, exercise variants and dosage remain unresolved.

sessions.progression_decision: Introduce the cue through an already stable position and teach retrieval. Retain simple lower-body work and reduce jumping after the prior instructional exposures.
sessions.prerequisites: OR-01 stop/start conduct or direct check; suitable implement, target, clear retrieval system and pain-free eligible upper-body position.
sessions.observation_recording: Record landing_throwing throw branch, cue_response release behavior and equipment handling independently of jump/braking status.

targeted_drill_purposes.purpose: Rehearse the stable throw start and push/pull shoulder-trunk positions with a light or unloaded pattern.

hypothetical_mid_block_pathway.starting_situation: A hypothetical 16-year-old arrives while the main group is in Week 6 and expects two weekly visits. The hypothetical intake identifies repeatable conduct, familiar preparation, simple acceleration/run-off and stable push/pull/brace; hinge and braking remain emerging; the separate tumbling coach has not yet recorded eligibility. pathway: First actual visit: verify the reported conduct/preparation/strength skills instead of accepting a self-rating. Use OR-02/OR-06 hinge teaching at the demonstrated level and retain familiar eligible full-body work. Do not add a missed week of instruction.

Next suitable visit: use OR-03 to observe a controlled straight stop and supported stance. If that is repeatable, OR-07 provides a paused predictable redirect route; if it is not, continue the straight-stop task only. Timing and total work remain within one normal visit.

At a later actual relevant visit, use OR-15/OR-19 hinge observation and OR-11/OR-20 braking review as needed. If the hypothetical observations are repeatable and current readiness is appropriate, record the exact passed variants. Otherwise keep only the unresolved branch instructional.

Join the main offering current when the relevant checks pass. On BRAKE use only the recorded straight stop or predictable redirect. On JUMP use a passed jump and hinge; if landing is still instructional, JUMP-T requires an independently passed familiar stable-throw gate through OR-05/OR-19 or direct evidence. While travel/braking remains instructional, REACT-T requires both that stable-throw gate and its actual early release rule through OR-05/OR-17, or separately demonstrated go/no-go through OR-09/OR-17. If those gates are unobserved or emerging, continue targeted instruction instead of assuming the substitute is safe. ACC retains its already verified start; RUN remains space-conditional. Record JUMP-T/REACT-T throws and cue behavior separately from jump or reactive-cut results.

Attach the first actual main Day ID and prescribed dose when chosen, linked to the actual OR evidence. Review that completed response before any increase. Obtain the separately managed tumbling foundation and prerequisites from its coach; the athlete does not restart the main program at Day 1 or receive advanced tumbling because of age.
hypothetical_mid_block_pathway.competency_logic: This is a conditional route, not a prediction of passes within a fixed number of visits. Mastered domains bypass teaching; unresolved domains retain targeted supervision. Exact loads, doses and canonical variants remain later-stage work. JUMP-T and REACT-T replace the regular main explosive plus complementary-throw allocation; they do not add a second throw block. Handoff uses the branch-specific main preparation, actual exposure chain, shoulder/strength/tumbling adjustments and compressed priorities.
